mcqs.learning_point: Relate ionic size to lattice properties
mcqs.question: Consider two ionic solids, NaCl and CsI. Which statement correctly compares their lattice energies based on ionic sizes?

options.A: NaCl has a higher lattice energy because both Na⁺ and Cl⁻ are smaller than Cs⁺ and I⁻ respectively.
options.B: CsI has a higher lattice energy because larger ions lead to stronger electrostatic attraction.
options.C: Both compounds have the same lattice energy because lattice energy depends only on the magnitude of the charges.
options.D: NaCl has a lower lattice energy because Na⁺ is smaller than Cs⁺.

mcqs.answer: NaCl has a higher lattice energy because both Na⁺ and Cl⁻ are smaller than Cs⁺ and I⁻ respectively.
mcqs.explanation: Lattice energy increases when the interacting ions are smaller, because the distance between the centers of the ions (r⁺ + r⁻) becomes smaller, leading to a stronger Coulombic attraction (U = k·Q⁺Q⁻/r). Na⁺ and Cl⁻ are considerably smaller than Cs⁺ and I⁻, so NaCl exhibits a larger lattice energy. Options B, C, and D misinterpret the size‑energy relationship.

mcqs.question: All of the following are characteristic properties of ionic compounds EXCEPT:

options.B: Good electrical conductivity in the solid state
options.C: Brittle nature and tendency to fracture on stress
options.D: Solubility in polar solvents such as water

mcqs.answer: Good electrical conductivity in the solid state
mcqs.explanation: Ionic solids conduct electricity only when molten or dissolved in water because ions become mobile. In the solid state, ions are fixed in the lattice, so they do not conduct. High melting points, brittleness, and solubility in polar solvents are typical ionic properties. Options A, C, and D correctly describe ionic compounds.

mcqs.learning_point: Explain formation of cations and anions
mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes how a cation is formed?

options.C: By sharing electrons equally with another atom

mcqs.explanation: A cation carries a positive charge because it has lost one or more electrons, reducing its electron count relative to protons. Gaining electrons forms an anion, while sharing electrons leads to covalent bonds, and nuclear fission is unrelated to ion formation.

mcqs.question: Ionic bond formation between Na and Cl involves which of the following steps?

options.A: Na transfers one electron to Cl, producing Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions that attract each other.
options.B: Both atoms share one electron each, forming a non‑polar covalent bond.
options.C: Cl transfers an electron to Na, giving Cl⁺ and Na⁻.
options.D: No electron transfer occurs; the atoms remain neutral.

mcqs.answer: Na transfers one electron to Cl, producing Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions that attract each other.
mcqs.explanation: In ionic bonding, the metal (Na) loses its valence electron, becoming Na⁺, while the non‑metal (Cl) gains that electron, becoming Cl⁻. The opposite charges create a strong electrostatic attraction, the ionic bond. Options B, C, and D describe incorrect mechanisms.

mcqs.question: Lattice energy is best defined as:

options.A: The energy released when one mole of an ionic solid is formed from its gaseous ions.
options.B: The energy required to break a covalent bond in a molecule.
options.C: The enthalpy change when a molecule dissociates into its constituent atoms.
options.D: The heat absorbed when a metal melts.

mcqs.answer: The energy released when one mole of an ionic solid is formed from its gaseous ions.
mcqs.explanation: Lattice energy (U) quantifies the strength of the ionic lattice; it is the exothermic energy change when gaseous cations and anions combine to form one mole of solid ionic compound. It differs from bond enthalpy, which pertains to covalent bonds (Option B). Options C and D describe unrelated processes.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate ionic size to lattice properties
mcqs.question: If the ionic radius of the cation in an ionic compound decreases while the anion radius remains constant, what is the expected effect on the lattice energy?
mcqs.explanation: Lattice energy is inversely proportional to the distance between ion centers (U ∝ 1/(r⁺+r⁻)). Reducing the cation radius shortens this distance, strengthening electrostatic attraction and raising lattice energy. Options B, C, and D contradict this relationship.

mcqs.question: NaCl is an ionic compound. Which property of NaCl best illustrates a typical behavior of ionic compounds?

options.A: It conducts electricity when dissolved in water.
options.B: It is a good conductor of electricity in the solid state.
options.C: It has a low melting point.
options.D: It is insoluble in polar solvents.

mcqs.answer: It conducts electricity when dissolved in water.
mcqs.explanation: When NaCl dissolves, Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions become mobile, allowing the solution to conduct electricity—a hallmark of ionic compounds. In the solid state, ionic lattices do not conduct (Option B). Ionic solids generally have high melting points (Option C) and are soluble in polar solvents like water (Option D is opposite).

mcqs.learning_point: Explain formation of cations and anions
mcqs.question: A metal atom X loses two electrons to form X²⁺ while a non‑metal atom Y gains two electrons to form Y²⁻. Which statement correctly explains this process?

options.A: X becomes a cation by losing electrons; Y becomes an anion by gaining electrons.
options.B: Both X and Y become cations.
options.C: Both X and Y become anions.
options.D: X gains electrons and Y loses electrons.

mcqs.answer: X becomes a cation by losing electrons; Y becomes an anion by gaining electrons.
mcqs.explanation: Cations are formed when atoms lose electrons, resulting in a positive charge (X²⁺). Anions are formed when atoms gain electrons, acquiring a negative charge (Y²⁻). Options B, C, and D invert or misstate the electron transfer direction.
